title: I just purchased my first ever asset for my game, do I give credit to them in the end game credits?
author: W3103_
selftext:
Made everything myself so far so not been a consideration. But after 10+ failed mermaid attempts I Have paid for a very nice asset and rig of a mermaid 

Paid for the full licensing for commercial use etc, have never made a game before so not aware of etiquette with stuff like this. 

Would you credit them? List as a contributing artist?  

Total hobbyist and amateur here so apologies if a dumb question

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: The credit rules will be with the asset. Look at the asset store page or the downloaded zip. It'll probably say you can use it however you want, just not redistribute it (as one asset) as if you made it. Another option is that it says you must credit the creator.

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: If its from a human artist it would be a nice thing to mention him even if its not parte of the licence

comments.author: Odd-Communication-18
comments.body: I would, even if it says no credit required, pays respect to the author

replies.author: W3103_
replies.body:
Building my whole game with Claude mate, built a load of tools to help me with it too. The mermaid was just too detailed for what I was after so was easier to spend a bit of money on a polished one. I’ve spent way too long trying to get it to look good. Wasting my tokens 

I was just asking about giving someone credit, no one here needs to know anything about the project to answer my question 

Trust me I ask Claude everything lol

comments.author: Davoguha2
comments.body:
Follow the license if provided, or ask the artist if you need clarity. 

I'd note, I've only worked with free assets - but some artists in that space specifically ask **not** to be credited. I.e. they're happy to share their models, but they don't want to be associated with random games in the wild. 

Might be different on commissions, but that's why licenses exist - if they want attribution or credit, there's a license for that.

comments.author: Dungrr
comments.body: Claude can read licenses. It caught a font I added that was personal license only and even suggested alternatives.

comments.author: Level3Super
comments.body: I need assets for a game, which site did you use please?

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body: Just make a credits section and follow the licensing terms
